notes:
350 names mapped (n=700-1049): 288 species, 18 genus, 21 family, 13 group, 10 unknown.

Where I departed from your instructions:
- "Hawk", "Hawks", "Grey Hawk", "Glede Hawk", "Holland Hawks" and "HAWES." are level group, not family. In these reports "hawk" also covers falcons ("Kestrel Hawk"; the committee thinks the "Glede Hawk" was a Peregrine), so neither Accipitridae nor Falconidae fits. Change it if you want a taxon anyway.
- "Geese" and "Goose" are group, because grey and black geese are two genera. "Grey Geese" is genus Anser.
- Paired names ("Golden and Grey Plover", "Great and Blue Titmouse", "Grey and Green Linnets", "Goldfinches or Linnets") are given at the lowest shared genus or family. Split them if your schema allows two species.

Check against your IOC version: Astur gentilis (Eurasian Goshawk) and Anarhynchus alexandrinus (Kentish Plover) follow IOC 14.x; Acanthis hornemanni (Arctic Redpoll) assumes the redpolls are still split. I also used Gulosus aristotelis, Curruca communis, Coloeus monedula, Western House Martin, Western Osprey, Eurasian Whimbrel and Common Murre.

Worth checking against the scans or context:
1. Garbles I couldn't read: Gaumnene (701), Giaren (704), Grey mee (844), Helios (900), land ade (1036), LanraDm. (1047), Herring Bird (911).
2. Bare fragments that need context per observation: "Grey" (826, 13 obs, could be Linnet, Plover, Crow or Geese), "Golden" (728), "Green" (805).
3. "Grey Linnets" (841, 118 obs): mapped to Common Linnet, but at Scottish island stations some may be Twite. The committee queries this in 842 and 843, which I put at genus Linaria.
4. "Golden Wrens" (742): mapped to Goldcrest; the August dates could be Willow Warblers.
5. Doubtful records you may want to flag: Harlequin Duck (882-883), flocks of Iceland Gulls (976), Great Shearwaters seen on a voyage to Algoa Bay (786, 799), "Jer Falcon" (998), quoted "Kingfishers" (1016), six harriers on a breakwater (884), and a "Gull" example with males and females (874), where the name may be matched to the wrong text.
6. Dialect names I'm only partly sure of: Green Bunting (808-809, the committee queries Greenfinch), Grey Wagtail flocks (855, maybe White Wagtails), Grey-headed Wagtail (865), Ground Lark (869), Grey Thrushes and Grey-birds (853, 863, perhaps Song Thrush), Lady Wagtail (1031), Golden/golden-headed Widgeon (741, 749), Horned Owl (948-949, genus Asio), Grouse (870, taken as Red Grouse), and House Swallow (959-960, taken as Barn Swallow, but maybe House Martin).
7. Heligoland Latin: hypolais (967) is taken as Icterine Warbler, haliaëtos (880) as Osprey, hortensis (950) as Garden Warbler, Hypolais pallida (969) as Eastern Olivaceous Warbler, and Hirundo (926) is kept at genus even though it may mean all hirundines.
8. Kagles (1000): family Accipitridae, almost certainly White-tailed Eagle in Shetland.
9. "Hoodpoe" (943): read as Hoopoe; check that it isn't Hooded Crow.
